newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICAN SUGAR MILLING MAY BE NORMALISED NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICAN SUGAR MILLING MAY BE NORMALISED NEXT WEEK.

text.p: South Africa's sugar milling and refining strike entered its second week on Wednesday, but an industry spokesman said there was a real possibility production could be normalised next week.

Some 4,000 workers at Illovo Sugar Ltd and Tongaat-Hulett Ltd are striking to push home their demands of a 20 percent wage increase, rejecting an employer offer of 10.5 percent. The strike began on July 2.

"The strike could be over by the end of the week, and we are working towards that by the middle of next week we can get production back to normal," spokesman for both companies, Bheki Sibiya, told Reuters.
He said negotiations with five unions representing the workers had been "fruitful" and that "significant progress had been made".
However, a union spokesman was not as optimistic.
"There is no sign that the employers want to address the gap in wages between ourselves and other agriculture-based industries," union spokesman Eric Botha told Reuters.

"They (the employers) might be in for a big surprise if they don't deliver the goods. The guys on the floor are very unhappy with what they have been offered and they are prepared to continue the strike for another week or two."
He said the unions had indicated in Tuesday's talks that they were prepared to move to a 15 percent wage increase, but that this had not been favourably received.
About 83,500 tonnes of cane per day were being lost, a sugar industry source said, but declined to put a value on the figure.

One of the options to deal with a backlog of uncut cane was to extend milling operations past Christmas, but the sucrose contents of the sugar would be lower, and the option was yet to be negotiated with growers, the source said.
